Order 
This is first application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant, as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No.700/2023, registered at P.S. Sarni, District Betul (M.P.)
for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) of IPC.

A s per prosecution story, prosecutrix lodged the FIR to this effect that applicant made assurance with her for solemnization of marriage and on the pretext of marriage, he committed sexual intercourse with her.
When the prosecutrix asked for marriage, the applicant refused to marry her.
Therefore, the case was registered against the applicant under aforesaid offence.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has not committed any offence and he has been falsely implicated in the crime.
He submitted that prosecutrix is married lady and she is not living with her husband.

It is further submitted that prosecutrix is the consenting party Deepak Uike vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105903119/
1 and she went with the applicant on her own will and lived with the applicant for four months.

sentences.text: There is no criminal record of the applicant.
Charge sheet has been filed and trial would take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer of the applicant for grant of bail.
Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the considered view that it is a fit case for grant of bail to the applicant.
Hence, without expressing any opinion on merits of the matter, application is allowed.

I t is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rs. Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court to appear before the court on the dates given by the concerned Court.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
